highlights: Budgets overlap well: Jake's $1,150-1,500 and Arjun's $1,200-1,500 share a $1,200-1,500 band, so rent is not a barrier.
Both are students looking in Fenway, moving in within 1-3 months, and wanting a 1-year lease. Logistics line up almost exactly.
Both are night owls who want to split utilities equally and split grocery basics, and both love pets but have none.
concerns: Jake smokes and Arjun requires a non-smoking household with no indoor smoking. This is a direct clash with Arjun's stated non-negotiable, and Arjun ended the conversation over it.

Arjun's non-negotiable is no parties ever, with guests once a month or less. Jake is social and lively and has guests weekly, and his top priorities are matching social energy and similar guest/party preferences.

Arjun works from home full-time and wants quiet and respect for work time. Jake's regular guests and social lifestyle would likely disrupt this, and the night-owl schedules add to the noise risk. Their cleanliness ratings also differ (2 vs 3).
analysis.dealbreaker_detail: Jake smokes, which conflicts with Arjun's non-negotiable of no indoor smoking. Jake's weekly guests and lively social style also clash with Arjun's non-negotiable of no parties ever. Arjun has already declared the match incompatible.
middle_ground: Only if Jake commits to smoking strictly outdoors, away from windows and entrances, with no smoke or odor indoors, might the smoking issue be revisited. Arjun has already ruled this out.
Jake would have to keep guests to a few low-key visits a month and hold gatherings elsewhere. This would likely conflict with Jake's own social priorities, so it probably isn't workable.
analysis.recommendation_summary: Budget, location, timing and lease expectations match well, but the lifestyle conflicts are fundamental. Jake's smoking and weekly social life run against Arjun's non-negotiables of no indoor smoking and no parties, and against his quiet full-time remote work. Arjun has declined, so this is not a viable match.
